catalog_quote: [Misnadin & Kirby 2018: 121-122] Word stress is an area that has not been systematically studied in Madurese. Impressionistically, word stress in both disyllabic and trisyllabic words occurs on the first syllable, while stress on words with four syllables appears to fall on the antepenultimate syllable. However, there is at present no phonetic evidence of word stress in Madurese, lexical or otherwise. ... [Kiliaan 1897 sec. 111, scanned] het accent heeft er geen vaste plaats; want bijkomende omstandigheden bewerken dat het nu eens op de voorlaatste dan weder op de laatste lettergreep wordt waargenomen. sources.quote: 'On Java itself, Javanese, Sundanese, Madurese and local varieties of Malay all appear to lack a consistent pattern of word stress ... Davies' (2010:51) description of the Madurese state of affairs seems to hold equally for other languages of Java: "Word stress is not a salient feature of Madurese, and receives little mention in the literature, e.g. Stevens (1968) mentions it only in passing. As pointed out by Ogloblin (1986), it is likely that the intonation group is the lowest relevant phonological unit in Madurese ... Words uttered in isolation exhibit stress on almost any syllable in the r
